findings.kind: unsupported critical engineering guarantee / missing run-input consistency condition
findings.claim: A clean replay can promise use of the recorded declared inputs and mark outputs current when input fingerprints still match, while declared data are live references exposed by read-only mounts.
findings.failure_condition: An independent writer changes a referenced dataset after its recorded fingerprint, the run reads the changed bytes, and the writer restores original bytes before commit verification. Read-only consumer permissions and project-write locks do not prevent this schedule.

primary_evidence.locator: Bind mount operation; read-only bind protects the new VFS mountpoint while the original filesystem/path may remain writable.

findings.limits: A deterministic isolated file schedule tests the proposed fingerprint inference, not a built app, actual bind mount, VM, DuckDB or Jupyter. The mount primary source supplies the live read-only-reference applicability. If a future backend provides immutable data snapshots or enforced exclusion, it can close this gap; the current final does not require that condition or classify mutable inputs unverified.
findings.required_constraint: Require one immutable/stable data epoch for the whole run or explicitly exclude uncontrolled live source mutation from current/replay guarantees and keep affected results unverified. Merely comparing digests before and at commit is insufficient.
findings.not_claimed: No assertion that DuckDB/Jupyter documentation is wrong or that a nonexistent full product was observed failing.

screening_rule: Decisive current guarantee gap; preserve all verified useful positive findings. Content coverage is mapped for every B obligation, but no full product/pipeline/matched causal PASS is asserted.
